questions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes a hazard from risk?
options: A hazard is the probability of injury, while risk is the unsafe condition
Hazard and risk are interchangeable terms in every assessment
A hazard is only an event that has already caused harm
A hazard is a source or condition with potential for harm; risk combines likelihood and consequence
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Hazard describes the potential source of harm. Risk estimates the chance and consequence of that harm under defined conditions.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Probability is one component of risk, not the definition of a hazard.
The terms describe different concepts and should not be treated as identical.
A hazard can exist before any incident occurs.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 26, definitions and risk-management process, pp. 604-606

questions.stem: A task has an occasional likelihood rating of 3 and a catastrophic consequence rating of 5. If the matrix multiplies likelihood by consequence, what is the initial risk score?
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Using the stated method, risk score = 3 x 5 = 15. The score must then be interpreted using the organization risk criteria.
incorrectOptionExplanations: This subtracts the ratings instead of combining them.
This adds the ratings rather than using the stated matrix method.
This squares the consequence rating and ignores likelihood.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 26, risk assessment scenario and risk ranking, pp. 606-610
questions.formula: risk score = likelihood rating x consequence rating

questions.stem: A risk assessment lists the hazard rating before controls and again after verified controls. What do the two ratings represent?
options: Compliance risk and financial risk
Inherent risk and residual risk
Acute risk and chronic risk
Transfer risk and insurance risk
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Inherent risk is estimated without relying on controls; residual risk is the risk remaining after controls are applied and verified.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Compliance and financial risks are different classifications and do not describe before-and-after control ratings.
Acute and chronic describe time course of effects, not control-state ratings.
Risk transfer is a treatment option, not the name for the two assessment states.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 26, control development, implementation, and evaluation, pp. 610-614

questions.stem: A solvent-cleaning process presents inhalation and fire hazards. Which proposal is the strongest risk treatment?
options: Issue half-mask respirators to all operators
Post additional warning signs near the process
Replace the solvent with a less hazardous validated cleaning method
Rotate operators every two hours
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A validated substitution reduces the hazard at its source and is stronger than controls that depend mainly on worker behavior.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Respirators are important when needed but depend on correct selection, fit, use, and program controls.
Warnings communicate risk but do not reduce the inherent hazard.
Rotation may reduce individual duration but leaves the hazard and exposes more people.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 26, controls development and decision-making, pp. 610-614

questions.stem: A team calls a high-consequence residual risk acceptable because no incident has occurred in five years. What is the main weakness?
options: Five years is always the minimum period required for acceptance
High-consequence hazards cannot ever be evaluated quantitatively
Residual risk should be based only on insurance premium
Past absence of loss does not demonstrate that residual risk meets defined acceptance criteria
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Acceptance should be based on approved criteria, control effectiveness, exposure, uncertainty, and consequence, not merely on a quiet loss history.
incorrectOptionExplanations: There is no universal five-year rule for deciding risk acceptability.
High-consequence hazards may be assessed using qualitative or quantitative methods with uncertainty stated.
Insurance cost does not replace technical and organizational risk criteria.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 26, risk evaluation and decision-making, pp. 604-614

questions.stem: Exposure data are sparse and the consequence could be severe. How should the uncertainty be handled?
options: Document assumptions, use a conservative decision where warranted, and obtain better data
Assign the lowest likelihood because no event was measured
Delete the hazard until a complete data set exists
Average the best and worst estimates without explanation
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A defensible assessment makes uncertainty visible, avoids false precision, and identifies additional data or interim controls.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Lack of evidence is not evidence of low likelihood.
Removing the hazard from the assessment hides uncertainty rather than managing it.
An unexplained average may falsely imply precision and conceal the range.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 26, hazard assessment and risk decision-making, pp. 606-614

questions.stem: Management asks for a one-page summary of a complex risk assessment. What information is essential?
options: Only the final color from the risk matrix
Hazard, exposed groups, assumptions, risk basis, controls, residual risk, and decision ownership
Only the names of employees who participated
Only the estimated financial cost of the preferred control
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A concise risk communication should preserve the evidence and assumptions needed to understand and act on the decision.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A color without context does not explain consequence, uncertainty, controls, or decision basis.
Participant names do not communicate the risk analysis.
Cost is one decision input and does not replace safety and health evidence.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 26, risk-management process and control decisions, pp. 604-614

questions.stem: In a bow-tie analysis, where are preventive and mitigative barriers placed?
options: Both barrier types are placed only after consequences occur
Preventive barriers are after consequences and mitigative barriers are before threats
Preventive barriers are before the top event; mitigative barriers are between the top event and consequences
Barrier placement is unrelated to the event sequence
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: The left side controls threats leading to loss of control; the right side limits escalation and consequences after the top event.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Barriers are intended to interrupt escalation before loss or reduce consequences after loss of control.
This reverses the role of the two barrier groups.
The method explicitly organizes threats, top event, barriers, and consequences.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 26 and Chapter 35, hazard-analysis and risk-control methods, pp. 604-614 and 791-795

questions.stem: A control decision changes depending on whether the assumed failure probability is 0.001 or 0.01. What should the analyst do?
options: Select the lower probability because it produces the preferred result
Report only the midpoint as the exact probability
Ignore probability and rank only by cost
Perform sensitivity analysis and identify which assumption drives the decision
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Sensitivity analysis tests how uncertainty in inputs affects the result and highlights where better evidence is most valuable.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Choosing the favorable assumption is biased and not evidence-based.
A midpoint can hide the fact that the conclusion changes across the plausible range.
Cost alone cannot represent the safety consequences and uncertainty.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 26, risk analysis and decision-making, pp. 606-614

questions.stem: What is the most accurate statement about transferring risk through insurance or contract?
options: Financial consequences may be transferred, but the organization still must control the underlying hazard
The hazard is eliminated when insurance is purchased
The contractor alone owns all risk once a contract is signed
Risk transfer replaces verification of controls
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Risk financing and contractual allocation can change who pays, but they do not remove the source of harm or the duty to manage it.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Insurance changes financing, not the physical condition that can cause harm.
Legal and operational duties may remain with multiple parties despite contract language.
Control verification is still needed because people remain exposed.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 26, risk-management options and decision-making, pp. 604-614

questions.stem: During a shutdown, the work conditions depart from the approved plan and an unanticipated chemical line is found. What is the best action?
options: Continue because the original risk assessment was approved
Pause the work, reassess the changed hazards, and authorize revised controls before continuing
Allow the most experienced worker to decide without documentation
Complete the task quickly to reduce exposure time
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Risk assessments must be revisited when conditions change so the control basis remains valid.
incorrectOptionExplanations: An assessment is not valid when critical assumptions and conditions have changed.
Experience helps, but significant changes require a controlled reassessment and authorization.
Speed can increase error and does not control unknown energy or chemical hazards.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 26, supervise and evaluate; Chapter 38, management of change, pp. 614 and 859-868

questions.stem: A ventilation control was installed for a high-priority exposure. What closes the risk-management loop?
options: Close the action when the purchase order is paid
Assume the design airflow is achieved because the fan is running
Measure performance and exposure to verify the control reduced risk as intended
Train employees to report symptoms and perform no technical check
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Implementation must be followed by effectiveness verification and continued monitoring where risk warrants it.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Administrative completion does not demonstrate control effectiveness.
Fan operation alone does not verify capture, flow, or exposure reduction.
Symptom reporting is reactive and cannot replace exposure and performance verification.
